Package com.benaether.rxon.core

Class Work<T>

java.lang.Object
com.benaether.rxon.core.Work<T>
public final class Work<T> extends Object
Work<T> is a lightweight, opinionated DSL built on top of RxJava Single for modeling synchronous and asynchronous units of work with explicit, semantic threading and composition rules.

This type represents a single, terminal computation that emits exactly one non-null value or an error.

Core principles

  • Exactly one value: Work<T> always emits exactly one value or fails (it is backed by Single).
  • No null values: Returning null from any transformation is illegal and will result in a NullPointerException thrown by RxJava.
  • Explicit threading: All execution happens on an explicitly provided WorkScheduler. Callers never manipulate raw Schedulers.
  • Semantic composition: Workflows encapsulate their own execution logic and threading. Callers only compose them; they never override internal schedulers.

Nullability rules (CRITICAL)

Never return null from any Work chain, including:

  • Sync chaining (on(...))
  • Async chaining (onAsync(...))
  • Workflow composition
  • Branching logic

RxJava does not permit null emissions. Violations will crash with:


 NullPointerException: The mapper function returned a null value

When absence of a value is valid

  • Return Optional<T>
  • Or return Unit for no-value workflows

 // CORRECT
 work.on(COMPUTE, value -> Optional.ofNullable(value));

 // INCORRECT (will crash)
 work.on(COMPUTE, value -> null);

Work<Void> warning

Void has no valid value and cannot be emitted safely.

  • Returning null will crash
  • Work<Void> should be avoided

Always prefer Unit for workflows that conceptually return no value.

Branching & conditional flow

Work supports explicit, first-class branching and early termination:

  • Conditional branching via branch(...) and branchAsync(...)
  • Early termination without failure via haltIf(...)
  • Fail-fast termination via failIf(...)

This enables a Railway-Oriented Programming style where:

  • Success continues the chain
  • Failures stop execution immediately
  • Errors are handled as early as possible

Execution

  • executeOn(WorkScheduler, Consumer, Consumer) executes the chain and delivers terminal callbacks on the provided scheduler.

Encapsulation rule

RxJava primitives (Single, Scheduler, etc.) are never exposed outside infrastructure boundaries.

All creation and composition must go through semantic DSL entry points such as on(...), onAsync(...), and workflows.

Intended usage

  • Repositories and services return Work<T>
  • ViewModels compose Work
  • UI layers execute and observe results

    • switchOn

      public <R> Work<R> switchOn(WorkScheduler scheduler, io.reactivex.rxjava3.functions.Function<T,Work<R>> decision)
      Perform controlled branching inside a Work chain.

      This operator allows dynamic selection of the next Work to execute based on the current value.

      Semantics

      • The provided decision function must return a non-null Work.
      • The returned Work determines how the chain continues.
      • If the returned Work fails, the entire chain fails.
      • If the returned Work completes normally, the chain continues with its result.

      Threading

      The branching decision itself runs on the provided WorkScheduler. The returned Work controls its own internal execution context.

      Typical use cases

      • Conditional workflow routing
      • Replacing nested flatMap pyramids
      • Guard-based branching
      • Early exit (via halt(Object) or fail(Throwable))

      Example

      
 Work.onAsync(IO, api.getUser())
     .switchOn(COMPUTE, user -> {
         if (!user.isActive()) {
             return Work.fail(new IllegalStateException("Inactive user"));
         }

         if (user.isGuest()) {
             return Work.halt(defaultProfile());
         }

         return loadFullProfile(user);
     });
      Type Parameters:
      R - result type of the next Work
      Parameters:
      scheduler - execution context for the branching decision
      decision - function that returns the next Work to execute
      Returns:
      new Work representing the selected branch
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the decision function returns null

    • halt

      public static <T> Work<T> halt(T value)
      Immediately terminate the current branch successfully with a value.

      This is a semantic early-return mechanism.

      Behavior

      • No further downstream operations in the original branch execute.
      • The chain continues from this returned Work.
      • No error is thrown.

      Important

      The value must not be null.

      Example

      
 if (cacheHit) {
     return Work.halt(cachedValue);
 }
      Type Parameters:
      T - type of value
      Parameters:
      value - non-null value to emit
      Returns:
      Work that immediately emits the value

    • fail

      public static <T> Work<T> fail(Throwable error)
      Immediately terminate the current branch with an error.

      This is a semantic failure mechanism used inside branching logic.

      Behavior

      • Stops further execution of the current chain.
      • Propagates the error downstream.
      • Will be delivered to the terminal executeOn(...) error handler.

      Example

      
 if (!authorized) {
     return Work.fail(new UnauthorizedException());
 }
      Type Parameters:
      T - expected type of Work
      Parameters:
      error - non-null Throwable
      Returns:
      Work that fails immediately
